title: Phase 8 · Cryptography & Blockchain
outline:
Phase 8 video (Algorithms, ECM3428): 'Cryptography & Blockchain', sub line 'How secrets and trust work online'. 11 scenes, about 122 s: title (4), the key problem (11), shared secret with paint (12), the same trick with numbers (15), RSA keys (12), RSA lock and unlock (12.2), a hash is a fingerprint (10), the hash chain (12.5), proof of work by guessing (13.5), rewriting costs work (11), recap (9). Story. SECRETS: a cipher needs a key, but Eve hears everything on the wire, so how can two strangers share a key? (1) Diffie-Hellman: each mixes a public value with a secret one and swaps the mixtures; each adds their own secret to what they received; both end with the SAME value and Eve cannot un-mix it (paint first, then numbers: x -> 5^x mod 23 is easy forwards and a hunt backwards). (2) RSA: Bob publishes a public key (n, e) that anyone can lock with, and keeps d; locking is 7 -> 13, unlocking 13 -> 7, and breaking it means factoring n (easy for n = 55, impossible for 617 digits). TRUST: (3) a hash is a short fingerprint of data (same data, same fingerprint; one letter changed, every digit changes; no way back); (4) a hash chain stores each block's predecessor's hash, so an edit breaks the next link, but a forger can recompute every later hash (detection, not prevention); (5) proof of work makes each block costly to seal (guess nonces until the hash starts with 0, 1 hash in 16; checking is one hash; every extra zero is 16 times rarer), so rewriting history means mining every later block again. Not covered (lessons 8.1 to 8.7 and the workshop): symmetric versus public-key comparison, XOR, frequency analysis, the man in the middle (Mallory), RSA limits (M below n, padding), Merkle roots, double spending, the longest chain and the 51 % attack, energy cost; the recap points to Workshop 8.W.

LESSONS the facts come from: a8-cipher 8.1 (shift cipher, key problem), a8-owf 8.2 (one-way functions), a8-keys 8.3 (paint picture, DH with p = 23, g = 5; RSA in miniature p = 5, q = 11), a8-rsa 8.4, a8-hash 8.5 (cat / cot, the chain runner), a8-bitcoin 8.6, a8-pow 8.7 (the mining runner), a8-chain 8.W (workshop); js/content/algo/algo-p8.js, algo-p8-x-01..04.js, algo-workshops-8-03.js; bank js/bank/algo-*.js (a8-*).

THE EXAMPLE DATA (all computed and asserted in videos/a8/common.js, a wrong number throws on page load). CIPHER: SECRET shifted by key 5 = XJHWJY (S->X E->J C->H R->W E->J T->Y). PAINT: public gold P, Alice's secret rose A, Bob's secret blue B; mixes P+A (orange) and P+B (green), both end with P+A+B (tan): the colour of a pot is the average of its paints, so the order does not matter. DIFFIE-HELLMAN (lesson 8.3 base table, not the p = 19 runner): p = 23, g = 5, a = 6, b = 15; A = 5^6 mod 23 = 8 (5^6 = 15625 = 679 x 23 + 8, which is how the video defines 'mod 23': the remainder after dividing by 23), B = 5^15 mod 23 = 19, Alice 19^6 mod 23 = 2, Bob 8^15 mod 23 = 2. Table 5^x mod 23 for x = 1..12: 5 2 10 4 20 8 17 16 11 9 22 18; Eve looking for x with 5^x mod 23 = 8 tries x = 1..6 (5 2 10 4 20 8) and hits at 6; a 2048-bit prime has 617 decimal digits (2^2048 - 1 starts 3231700607131100). RSA (lesson 8.3 'RSA in miniature'): p = 5, q = 11, n = 55, z = (5-1)(11-1) = 40, e = 3 (gcd(3, 40) = 1; 2 shares the factor 2), d = 27 (3 x 27 = 81 = 2 x 40 + 1); message 7: 7^3 = 343 = 6 x 55 + 13 so C = 13; 13^27 mod 55 = 7; Eve divides 55 by 2, 3, 4, 5 and finds 5 x 11, then z = 40 and d = 27. HASH (the lesson's toy 32-bit hash, 8 hex digits): cat = f01dce9c, cot = cb26b6bb (all 8 digits differ, 18 of 32 bits). CHAIN (lesson 8.5 runner, hash = toy(i|data|prev)), genesis hash ecaf011a: block 1 'ann pays ben 5' prev ecaf011a hash fb28ccb9; block 2 'ben pays cat 2' prev fb28ccb9 hash 51320862; block 3 'cat pays dan 1' prev 51320862 hash 57cc211e. Edit block 1 to 'ann pays EVE 50': hash 9a1f8189, block 2's stored prev fb28ccb9 now mismatches; repaired: block 2 hash 25ebb100, block 3 mismatches; repaired: block 3 hash 99c1e647 (a valid-looking forged chain). MINING (lesson 8.7 runner): block 7 'cat pays dan 4', target 'hash starts with 0': nonces 0..14 give cfc7cb5a 7d987054 66de0aae 72030365 d0998061 8499c79e 5e9431de d7cebafb 5510bdc2 33f2b038 d0cb0883 dd0f6394 be6270a4 2c063bfb 0d84059e, so it is found at nonce 14 after 15 hashes; checking costs 1 hash; one hash in 16 starts with 0, one in 256 with 00. REWRITING (the same three blocks, now sealed by mining with hash input 'block i|data|prev|nonce n'; the hashes therefore differ from scene 8, which has no nonce): sealed nonces 27 / 24 / 16 (hashes 017b7e46 / 0b2e58f5 / 006f9014); after the edit block 1 keeps nonce 27 but its hash is b411b36a (no leading 0: seal broken) and block 2's prev is stale; re-mined: block 1 nonce 14 (15 tries, hash 03fbf4ca), block 2 nonce 4 (5 tries, hash 06ab4a15), block 3 nonce 29 (30 tries, hash 0e76a113): 50 tries in all.

VIDEO-WIDE CONVENTIONS. COLOURS (whole video, see the outline): blue = PUBLIC (anything Eve can see: public numbers, the public key, what crosses the wire, fingerprints); purple = SECRET (private numbers, keys and paint, always with a lock icon or a dashed purple frame); green = agreed / valid / unlocked / sealed; red = Eve and everything broken (her disc and copies, a mismatching link, a failed guess); orange = attention (what changed, the guesses being tried); grey = neutral. Symbols (ticks, crosses, arrows, locks, keys, eyes, the equals sign, question marks) are SVG pictograms (A8.icon, L5.arrow), never glyphs; arithmetic signs inside numbers (x, +, -, =, the division sign) are plain text. Characters: Alice = grey letter disc A (A8.person who 'alice', stage (52, 48), name to its right), Bob = grey disc B ((884, 48), name to its left), Eve = solid red disc E (who 'eve'; always in the lower part of the stage, centred at (468, 578) in scenes 2 and 3, left at (52, 520) in scene 6, top-left (52, 48) in the second half of scene 4). THE OPEN WIRE (scenes 2, 3, 4, 6): a pale rounded band, A8.wire, between Alice's side and Bob's side; everything that travels along it is visible to Eve. In scenes 3, 4 and 6 the 'working spots' are (110, 190) for Alice and (826, 190) for Bob and the wire is x 150..786 at y 190 (heights 176, 120, 90); secrets are always kept BELOW the wire (scene 3 y 380, scene 4 y 430) with a lock icon or purple frame, and never travel. Mixtures / values that travel pass each other on arcs (A8.arc with bend +42 for Alice's, -42 for Bob's). Exponents: A8.pow(base, exp, fs) puts the exponent at 28 px or more (use fs 40 or 44 for expressions), so no label is under 28 px. Hashes and nonces are monospace (A8.digest, A8.block). Chain blocks (scenes 8, 10) are A8.block cards 270 px wide at x 0 / 333 / 666. The fingerprints on screen are the lesson's toy hash, full 8 hex digits. Scenes 3 and 4 mirror each other (same people, wire, spots and secrets) so the viewer sees the numbers as the same trick as the paint. A8.PAINT paints are literal colours (gold, rose and blue tokens; the mixtures are computed averages of those tokens, as paint is), the only place colour is not a role; the purple dashed frame still marks secret paint and the blue frame public paint. The title card headline is 72 px (scene-01-title.js is finished: a copy of VID.titleCard with a smaller headline) because 'Cryptography & Blockchain' is wider than the 92 px of VID.titleCard; do not replace it.

title: The cipher needs a key
but Eve is listening
caps: Anything on the open wire, Eve can read.
A cipher scrambles it with a secret key.
But how does Bob get the key without Eve seeing it?
scenes.spec:
IDEA: Alice wants to send Bob SECRET. Everything on the wire can be copied by Eve. A cipher scrambles the letters with a secret KEY (shift each letter 5 along), but Bob needs the same key, and sending it over the same wire lets Eve copy it too. That is the key problem the rest of the phase solves. COLOURS (whole video, see the outline): blue = PUBLIC (anything Eve can see: public numbers, the public key, what crosses the wire, fingerprints); purple = SECRET (private numbers, keys and paint, always with a lock icon or a dashed purple frame); green = agreed / valid / unlocked / sealed; red = Eve and everything broken (her disc and copies, a mismatching link, a failed guess); orange = attention (what changed, the guesses being tried); grey = neutral.

LAYOUT (stage px, 936 x 640). Alice = A8.person(stage, {who: 'alice', x: 52, y: 48}), Bob = A8.person(stage, {who: 'bob', x: 884, y: 48, name: 'left'}). THE WIRE: A8.wire(stage, {x: 40, y: 215, w: 856, h: 150}) (a band y 140..290 with two lanes: letters travel in the upper lane y 190, the key in the lower lane y 258) and a label A8.tag(stage, {x: 468, y: 112, text: 'the open wire'}) above it. THE MESSAGE: const msg = L5.chromosome(stage, {x: 62, y: 162, genes: 'SECRET', size: 56, gap: 8, tone: 'grey'}) (six 56 px tiles, 376 px wide, tile centres x 90 + 64 i, y 190); msg.all((i) => ({x: dx, o, ...})) slides it (dx 0 = at Alice's end, +218 = centre of the wire, +432 = Bob's end, tile centres 522..842); msg.flip(i, k, {from: A8.CIPHER.pairs[i].from, to: A8.CIPHER.pairs[i].to, tone: 'grey', toTone: 'blue', x: dx}) turns S E C R E T into X J H W J Y (grey = readable, blue = scrambled and public). '+5' labels: six A8.tag(stage, {x: 90 + 64 i, y: 246, text: '+5', tone: 'orange', w: 52, h: 40}). ALICE'S KEY: A8.icon(stage, 'key', {x: 56, y: 370, tone: 'purple', size: 64}) and A8.tag(stage, {x: 160, y: 370, text: 'key 5', tone: 'purple', fs: 36}). BOB'S MISSING KEY: A8.tag(stage, {x: 766, y: 370, text: 'key ?', ghost: true, fs: 36}) with A8.icon(stage, 'qmark', {x: 860, y: 370, tone: 'orange', size: 56}). THE TRAVELLING KEY: a second A8.tag(stage, {text: 'key 5', tone: 'purple', fs: 36}) moved with A8.along([[160, 370], [160, 258], [700, 258]], f). EVE: A8.person(stage, {who: 'eve', x: 468, y: 578}), A8.icon(stage, 'eye', {x: 468, y: 495, tone: 'red'}), her copy of what passes: L5.chromosome(stage, {x: 280, y: 392, genes: 'SECRET' (then 'XJHWJY'), size: 56, gap: 8, tone: 'red'}) or for the key A8.tag(stage, {x: 468, y: 420, text: 'key 5', tone: 'red', solid: true, fs: 36}); a red 'copy' arrow A8.link(stage, {pts: [[468, 295], [468, 390]], tone: 'red'}) (for the key use pts [[700, 295], [700, 340], [468, 340], [468, 390]]); a red A8.icon(stage, 'qmark', {x: 700, y: 420, tone: 'red', size: 50}) next to her copy of the scrambled letters (she cannot read it).

DATA (assert with A8.same): A8.CIPHER = {plain 'SECRET', key 5, cipher 'XJHWJY', pairs S->X E->J C->H R->W E->J T->Y}. msg tiles read A8.CIPHER.plain then A8.CIPHER.cipher.

TIMELINE (local seconds). 0.2-0.8 Alice and Bob pop (k = ramp), the wire grows (wire.set({k: ramp(t, 0.2, 0.9)})), the label pops at 0.7. 0.9-1.4 the six grey tiles pop at Alice's end (0.06 s apart). 1.5-2.4 the tiles slide to the middle of the wire (dx 0 -> 218, ease inOut). 2.4-2.8 the red copy arrow draws (link k) and 2.7-3.1 Eve's red copy row 'SECRET' pops, 3.0 the eye pops and Eve pops (0.25 s each). 3.1-4.0 hold. 4.0-4.5 the plain row (on the wire), Eve's copy, her arrow and eye fade out (o), the row returns to dx 0 (hidden while it moves back). 4.4-5.0 the row pops again at Alice's end in grey; the key icon and 'key 5' tag pop (purple). 5.0-6.6 the six tiles flip one after another (flip starts 5.0 + 0.14 i, each 0.35 s), each '+5' tag pops 0.1 s before its tile flips, the tiles turn blue. 6.8-7.8 the '+5' tags fade, the blue row slides to Bob's end (dx 0 -> 432); at 7.4 the red copy arrow draws and Eve's red row 'XJHWJY' pops 7.4-7.9 with the red qmark at 7.8. 8.0-8.6 the row at Bob's end stays; Bob's ghost 'key ?' tag and orange qmark pop (8.2). 8.4 Eve's copy row, arrow and qmark fade out. 8.8-10.0 the travelling purple 'key 5' copy follows the polyline (f = ramp(t, 8.8, 10.0, inOut)) up to the lower lane and right to Bob's end; at 9.6 the arrow [[700,295],[700,340],[468,340],[468,390]] draws and at 9.9 Eve's red solid 'key 5' tag and the eye pop. 10.0-10.8 hold.

END STATE: Alice's purple key beside her, the blue cipher row and the purple key copy at Bob's end of the wire, Bob's ghost 'key ?', Eve with a solid red 'key 5' copy: she has the key too. Scene 3 answers the question. CAPTIONS: [[2.0,4.2,"Anything on the open wire, Eve can read."],[5.0,7.2,"A cipher scrambles it with a secret key."],[8.7,10.8,"But how does Bob get the key without Eve seeing it?"]]

title: Mix paint in public,
share a secret colour
caps: Both start with the same public paint.
Each adds a secret paint of their own.
They swap the mixtures. Eve can see those.
Each adds their own secret again: the very same colour.
Eve cannot unmix paint to find a secret.
scenes.spec:
IDEA: the paint picture of Diffie-Hellman. Alice and Bob start with the same PUBLIC paint, each adds a SECRET paint, they swap the mixtures in public, each adds their own secret to the mixture they received, and both hold the same colour. Mixing is easy, unmixing is not, so Eve (who sees both mixtures) cannot make that colour. COLOURS (whole video, see the outline): blue = PUBLIC (anything Eve can see: public numbers, the public key, what crosses the wire, fingerprints); purple = SECRET (private numbers, keys and paint, always with a lock icon or a dashed purple frame); green = agreed / valid / unlocked / sealed; red = Eve and everything broken (her disc and copies, a mismatching link, a failed guess); orange = attention (what changed, the guesses being tried); grey = neutral. In this scene only, paints are literal colours: public = gold, Alice's secret = rose (red), Bob's secret = blue; a pot's colour is the average of its paints (A8.pot does the mixing).

LAYOUT (stage px). Alice = A8.person(stage, {who: 'alice', x: 52, y: 48}), Bob = A8.person(stage, {who: 'bob', x: 884, y: 48, name: 'left'}); label A8.tag(stage, {x: 468, y: 66, text: 'the open wire'}); THE PIPE: A8.wire(stage, {x: 150, y: 190, w: 636, h: 176}) (band y 102..278). WORKING POTS (they sit at the pipe's two ends and are the ones that change colour and swap): alicePot = A8.pot(stage, {x: 110, y: 190, r: 40}), bobPot = A8.pot(stage, {x: 826, y: 190, r: 40}); pot.set({drops: [...], frame: 'blue', frameK, x, y, s, o, k}). SECRET POTS (never move): A8.pot(stage, {x: 110, y: 380, r: 40}) with drops ['A'] and frame 'purple', A8.pot(stage, {x: 826, y: 380, r: 40}) with drops ['B'] and frame 'purple'. LABELS: A8.tag(stage, {x: 110, y: 275, text: 'public', tone: 'blue'}) and (826, 275) (change the text to 'mix' once the pot is mixed), A8.tag(stage, {x: 110, y: 455, text: 'secret', tone: 'purple'}) and (826, 455). DROPS: A8.drop(stage, {r: 18}) with set({paint: 'A', x, y}) following A8.arc({x: 110, y: 380}, {x: 110, y: 190}, f, 0) (Alice's rose drop rises into her pot), 'B' on the right (826). EVE: A8.person(stage, {who: 'eve', x: 468, y: 578}), A8.icon(stage, 'eye', {x: 468, y: 490, tone: 'red'}); her copies are small pots A8.pot(stage, {x: 400, y: 410, r: 32}) with drops A8.PAINT.mixA (orange) and A8.pot(stage, {x: 536, y: 410, r: 32}) with drops A8.PAINT.mixB (green); between them A8.icon(stage, 'qmark', {x: 468, y: 410, tone: 'red', size: 50}). THE RESULT: A8.icon(stage, 'equals', {x: 468, y: 190, tone: 'green', disc: true, size: 64}).

DATA (assert with A8.same): A8.PAINT = {paints {P gold, A rose, B blue}, mixA ['P','A'], mixB ['P','B'], finalAlice ['P','B','A'], finalBob ['P','A','B'] (the same multiset, so the same colour), eveSees}. Pot states: Alice's working pot ['P'] -> mixA -> (after the swap she holds Bob's) mixB -> finalAlice; Bob's ['P'] -> mixB -> mixA -> finalBob.

TIMELINE. 0.2-1.0 Alice and Bob pop, the pipe grows (0.3-1.0), the label pops 0.8. 1.0-1.8 the two public pots pop (gold, k = ramp), their blue frames pop (frameK 1.4-1.8), the 'public' tags pop 1.6. 3.4-4.0 the two secret pots pop with purple frames, the 'secret' tags pop 3.9. 4.4-5.0 the secret drops (rose left, blue right) rise from the secret pots into the working pots (A8.arc, f = ramp(t, 4.4, 5.0, inOut)), at 5.0 the pots take their mixes (orange on the left, green on the right, with a small pop s 1.15), the tags change to 'mix'; the secret pots stay full. 5.8-7.0 the swap: Alice's orange pot goes from (110,190) to (826,190) with A8.arc(..., f, 42) (arcs up), Bob's green pot the other way with bend -42 (arcs down) (f = ramp(t, 5.8, 7.0, inOut)); they never touch. 6.0 Eve pops, 6.3-6.8 her two small copies pop (orange and green) and the eye pops 6.6. 7.7-8.3 the second drops: Alice's rose drop rises into the green pot she now holds, Bob's blue drop into the orange pot he now holds; at 8.3 both pots turn tan (finalAlice / finalBob, the same colour) with a small pop. 8.8-9.3 the green equals disc pops between them at (468, 190). 10.1-10.6 Eve's red qmark pops between her two copies (with a short shake: dx = 6 sin).

END STATE: two identical tan pots joined by a green equals sign, the secret pots (rose, blue) untouched in purple frames, Eve with her orange and green copies and a red question mark. Scene 4 repeats the exchange with numbers. CAPTIONS: [[1.2,3.4,"Both start with the same public paint."],[3.6,5.8,"Each adds a secret paint of their own."],[6.0,8.0,"They swap the mixtures. Eve can see those."],[8.0,9.9,"Each adds their own secret again: the very same colour."],[10.1,11.8,"Eve cannot unmix paint to find a secret."]]

title: The same trick
with numbers
caps: Public: p = 23 and g = 5. Secret: a = 6 and b = 15.
mod 23 keeps only the remainder after dividing by 23.
They swap A = 8 and B = 19 in public.
Both get 2. The secret numbers were never sent.
Eve must try every power of 5 until she hits 8.
A 617-digit prime makes that search hopeless.
scenes.spec:
IDEA: the same exchange with numbers (lesson 8.3). Public p = 23 and g = 5; Alice keeps a = 6, Bob keeps b = 15; Alice sends A = 5^6 mod 23 = 8, Bob sends B = 5^15 mod 23 = 19; Alice computes 19^6 mod 23 = 2 and Bob 8^15 mod 23 = 2: the same number, and the secrets never crossed the wire. 'mod 23' is DEFINED on screen as the remainder after dividing by 23 (5^6 = 15625 = 679 x 23 + 8). The second half shows why Eve is stuck: to find a she must hunt through 5^x mod 23 (6 tries here) and with a 617-digit prime the hunt cannot finish. COLOURS (whole video, see the outline): blue = PUBLIC (anything Eve can see: public numbers, the public key, what crosses the wire, fingerprints); purple = SECRET (private numbers, keys and paint, always with a lock icon or a dashed purple frame); green = agreed / valid / unlocked / sealed; red = Eve and everything broken (her disc and copies, a mismatching link, a failed guess); orange = attention (what changed, the guesses being tried); grey = neutral.

LAYOUT, FIRST HALF (the exchange; it mirrors scene 3). Alice = A8.person(stage, {who: 'alice', x: 52, y: 48}), Bob (884, 48, name 'left'). Public tags A8.tag(stage, {x: 390, y: 66, text: 'p = 23', tone: 'blue', fs: 36}) and ({x: 545, y: 66, text: 'g = 5', ...}). THE PIPE: A8.wire(stage, {x: 150, y: 190, w: 636, h: 120}). WORKING SPOTS (they sit at the pipe's two ends, like the pots of scene 3): A8.tag(stage, {x: 110, y: 190, text: 'A = 8', tone: 'blue', solid: true, fs: 40}) for Alice and ({x: 826, y: 190, text: 'B = 19', ...}) for Bob; they swap places along the pipe with A8.arc(p, q, f, +36 for Alice's, -36 for Bob's). SECRETS (below the pipe, never move): A8.tag(stage, {x: 130, y: 430, text: 'a = 6', tone: 'purple', fs: 36}) with A8.icon(stage, 'lock', {x: 46, y: 430, tone: 'purple', size: 50}); A8.tag(stage, {x: 806, y: 430, text: 'b = 15', ...}) with the lock at (890, 430). THE MOD DEFINITION: panel A8.tag(stage, {x: 468, y: 520, tone: 'orange', fs: 40, box: true}) whose html is A8.pow('5', '6') + ' = 15625 = 679 × 23 + 8' (type it with V.type), and under it A8.tag(stage, {x: 468, y: 590, text: 'mod 23 = the remainder 8', tone: 'orange', solid: true}). RESULTS: A8.tag(stage, {x: 170, y: 330, tone: 'green', fs: 40, box: true}) with html A8.pow('19', '6', 40) + ' mod 23 = 2' and ({x: 766, y: 330}) with A8.pow('8', '15', 40) + ' mod 23 = 2'; between them A8.icon(stage, 'equals', {x: 468, y: 330, tone: 'green', disc: true, size: 64}).
LAYOUT, SECOND HALF (Eve's hunt; everything of the first half has faded). A8.person(stage, {who: 'eve', x: 52, y: 48}); Eve's known numbers A8.tag(stage, {y: 48, fs: 32, tone: 'blue'}) at x 285 'p = 23', 425 'g = 5', 545 'A = 8', 665 'B = 19', and A8.tag(stage, {x: 810, y: 48, text: 'a = ?', tone: 'purple', ghost: true, fs: 32}); the question A8.tag(stage, {x: 468, y: 150, tone: 'orange', fs: 40, box: true}) with html A8.pow('5', 'x') + ' mod 23 = 8, so x = ?'; the six tries A8.tag(stage, {x: 178 + 116 i, y: 280, text: 'x = ' + s.x + '\n' + s.y, box: true, w: 104, h: 96, fs: 30, tone: 'orange'}) for s = A8.DH.search[i] (the last one tone 'green'); 'tries' A8.tag(stage, {x: 468, y: 375, text: '6 tries', tone: 'green', solid: true, fs: 36}); the big number A8.tag(stage, {x: 300, y: 500, text: A8.BIG.lead + ' ...', tone: 'blue', mono: true, fs: 36}) and A8.tag(stage, {x: 690, y: 500, text: 'a real p: 617 digits', tone: 'blue', solid: true, fs: 32}); finally A8.tag(stage, {x: 468, y: 580, text: 'no computer can search that', tone: 'red', fs: 32}).

DATA (assert with A8.same): A8.DH = {p 23, g 5, a 6, b 15, A 8, B 19, shared 2, powA 15625, quot 679, rem 8, aliceCalc {base 19, exp 6, result 2}, bobCalc {base 8, exp 15, result 2}, table [5,2,10,4,20,8,17,16,11,9,22,18], search [{x 1, y 5} {x 2, y 2} {x 3, y 10} {x 4, y 4} {x 5, y 20} {x 6, y 8, hit}], tries 6, digits2048 617}; A8.BIG = {digits 617, lead '3231700607131100'}.

TIMELINE. 0.2-0.9 persons pop, the pipe grows. 0.5-1.1 'p = 23' and 'g = 5' pop (blue). 1.2-1.8 'a = 6' and 'b = 15' pop with their locks (purple). 3.6-3.9 the definition panel pops; 3.8-4.8 its text types out (V.type of ' = 15625 = 679 × 23 + 8' after the raised 5^6); 4.9 the orange 'mod 23 = the remainder 8' tag pops; 5.5 'A = 8' pops at Alice's spot (solid blue, s 1.15 pop), 5.7 'B = 19' pops at Bob's spot; 5.9-6.1 the panel and its tag fade. 6.2-7.4 the swap: A8.arc with bend +36 (Alice's A = 8 goes right) and -36 (B = 19 goes left), f = ramp(t, 6.2, 7.4, inOut). 7.6-8.1 Alice's green result 'A8.pow(19, 6) mod 23 = 2' pops at (170, 330) (the received tag B = 19 and her a = 6 flash once at 7.5), 7.8-8.3 Bob's pops at (766, 330); 8.6-9.0 the equals disc pops. 9.2-10.2 hold. 10.2-10.6 everything of the first half fades out. 10.7-11.2 Eve pops and her blue tags and the ghost 'a = ?' pop 0.08 s apart; 11.0 the orange question pops; 11.3-12.8 the six tries pop one by one, 0.3 s apart (11.3 + 0.3 i), each in orange; the last (x = 6, value 8) turns green with a pop (12.8). 13.0 '6 tries' pops. 13.3 the long number tag pops, 13.6 'a real p: 617 digits', 13.9 the red 'no computer can search that'. 14.0-14.8 hold.

END STATE: Eve with six tries ending in a green hit, '6 tries' in green, and next to it the 617-digit number she could never hunt through (red tag). Scene 5 starts RSA. CAPTIONS: [[0.6,3.4,"Public: p = 23 and g = 5. Secret: a = 6 and b = 15."],[3.8,6.0,"mod 23 keeps only the remainder after dividing by 23."],[6.2,7.8,"They swap A = 8 and B = 19 in public."],[8.0,10.2,"Both get 2. The secret numbers were never sent."],[10.9,13.0,"Eve must try every power of 5 until she hits 8."],[13.2,14.8,"A 617-digit prime makes that search hopeless."]]

title: Publish a lock,
keep the key
caps: Pick two secret primes: 5 and 11.
Multiply them: n = 55 will be public.
Next z = (5 − 1) × (11 − 1) = 40, kept secret.
Pick e = 3: it shares no factor with 40.
Publish (55, 3). Keep 27 secret.
scenes.spec:
IDEA: building a toy RSA key pair (lesson 8.3 'RSA in miniature'). Bob picks two secret primes p = 5 and q = 11, multiplies them to n = 55 (public), computes z = (5 - 1)(11 - 1) = 40 (secret), picks e = 3 which shares no factor with 40 (public), and finds d = 27 with 3 x 27 = 81 = 2 x 40 + 1 (secret). He publishes the PUBLIC KEY (55, 3), drawn as a padlock anyone can snap shut, and keeps the PRIVATE KEY 27, drawn as the only key that opens it. COLOURS (whole video, see the outline): blue = PUBLIC (anything Eve can see: public numbers, the public key, what crosses the wire, fingerprints); purple = SECRET (private numbers, keys and paint, always with a lock icon or a dashed purple frame); green = agreed / valid / unlocked / sealed; red = Eve and everything broken (her disc and copies, a mismatching link, a failed guess); orange = attention (what changed, the guesses being tried); grey = neutral.

LAYOUT (stage px). Bob = A8.person(stage, {who: 'bob', x: 52, y: 48}). THE RECIPE is a left column of rows, each an A8.tag(stage, {tone, fs, anchor: 'l'}): row 1 (y 130) A8.tag(stage, {x: 140, y: 130, text: 'p = 5', tone: 'purple', fs: 40}) and ({x: 290, y: 130, text: 'q = 11', ...}) (anchor 'c'); row 2 (x 20, y 225) 'n = 5 × 11 = 55' blue fs 40; row 3 (x 20, y 320) 'z = (5−1) × (11−1) = 40' purple fs 36; row 4 (x 20, y 415) 'e = 3' blue fs 40, then A8.tag(stage, {x: 190, y: 415, text: 'shares no factor with 40', tone: 'green', anchor: 'l'}) with A8.icon(stage, 'tick', {x: 560, y: 415, tone: 'green', size: 44}); row 5 (x 20, y 510) 'd = 27' purple fs 40, then A8.tag(stage, {x: 220, y: 510, text: '3 × 27 = 81 = 2 × 40 + 1', tone: 'purple', fs: 32, anchor: 'l'}). THE KEY PAIR is a right column centred at x 740: A8.icon(stage, 'lock', {x: 740, y: 190, tone: 'blue', size: 120}), A8.tag(stage, {x: 740, y: 290, text: 'public key', tone: 'blue', fs: 32}), A8.tag(stage, {x: 740, y: 345, text: '(55, 3)', tone: 'blue', solid: true, fs: 36}); A8.icon(stage, 'key', {x: 740, y: 440, tone: 'purple', size: 120}), A8.tag(stage, {x: 740, y: 540, text: 'private key', tone: 'purple', fs: 32}), A8.tag(stage, {x: 740, y: 595, text: '27', tone: 'purple', solid: true, fs: 36}).

DATA (assert with A8.same): A8.RSA = {p 5, q 11, n 55, z 40, e 3, d 27, eCands [{e 2, g 2}, {e 3, g 1}], dCheck {prod 81, k 2, rem 1}}. The row texts come from these numbers (build them from A8.RSA, not by hand).

TIMELINE. 0.2-0.7 Bob pops. 0.6-1.4 'p = 5' then 'q = 11' pop (0.2 s apart). 1.8-2.6 row 2 pops (blue) and the blue 'n' flashes once. 3.0-3.8 row 3 pops (purple). 5.2-5.8 row 4's 'e = 3' pops, 5.8-6.4 the green 'shares no factor with 40' tag pops and its tick draws on (A8.icon draw). 6.8-7.4 'd = 27' pops, 7.2-7.9 the relation tag pops and its '+ 1' is the last part to appear (type it, V.type). 8.8-9.2 the secret rows p, q, z fade to o 0.35 (they are forgotten, only the keys leave). 9.6-10.3 the blue padlock pops (s 0.8 -> 1 pop) and its two tags pop; 10.2-10.9 the purple key pops and its two tags pop. 11.0-11.6 hold (the padlock does a small bump at 10.4, V.flash).

END STATE: the whole recipe on the left (secret rows dimmed), on the right the blue public padlock with (55, 3) and the purple private key with 27. Scene 6 uses them. Keep 27 secret."]]

title: Anyone can lock it,
only Bob can unlock
caps: Bob shares his public key, (55, 3).
Alice locks 7 with it and gets 13.
Bob unlocks 13 with his private key: back to 7.
Eve factors the tiny n in four tries: 5 × 11.
A real n has 617 digits.
scenes.spec:
IDEA: using the key pair of scene 5. Bob sends out his public key (55, 3); Alice locks her message 7 with it: 7^3 = 343 = 6 x 55 + 13, so she sends 13; Bob unlocks with d = 27: 13^27 mod 55 = 7. Eve sees (55, 3) and 13 but not 27; to get it she must factor n: dividing 55 by 2, 3, 4, 5 she finds 5 x 11 in four tries, then z = 40 and d = 27: the toy key is broken, which is why a real n has 617 digits. COLOURS (whole video, see the outline): blue = PUBLIC (anything Eve can see: public numbers, the public key, what crosses the wire, fingerprints); purple = SECRET (private numbers, keys and paint, always with a lock icon or a dashed purple frame); green = agreed / valid / unlocked / sealed; red = Eve and everything broken (her disc and copies, a mismatching link, a failed guess); orange = attention (what changed, the guesses being tried); grey = neutral. LAYOUT (stage px). Alice (52, 48), Bob (884, 48, name 'left'). A8.wire(stage, {x: 150, y: 190, w: 636, h: 90}). ALICE'S MESSAGE at her working spot (110, 190): A8.tag(stage, {x: 110, y: 190, text: '7', tone: 'grey', fs: 48, box: true, w: 80, h: 80}); it becomes the locked value A8.tag(... text '13', tone 'blue', solid: true ...) with a small closed A8.icon(stage, 'lock', {x: 150, y: 150, tone: 'purple', size: 44}) at its top-right corner, travels along the wire to Bob's spot (826, 190) (A8.along([[110,190],[826,190]], f)), opens the lock (A8.icon .set({open})) and turns into A8.tag(... text '7', tone 'green', solid: true ...). BOB'S KEYS (right column): A8.icon(stage, 'lock', {x: 730, y: 300, tone: 'blue', size: 56}) with A8.tag(stage, {x: 840, y: 300, text: '(55, 3)', tone: 'blue', fs: 36}); A8.icon(stage, 'key', {x: 730, y: 390, tone: 'purple', size: 64}) with A8.tag(stage, {x: 830, y: 390, text: '27', tone: 'purple', solid: true, fs: 36}). ALICE'S COPY of the public key (left): A8.icon(stage, 'lock', {x: 130, y: 300, tone: 'blue', size: 56}) and A8.tag(stage, {x: 240, y: 300, text: '(55, 3)', tone: 'blue', fs: 36}). THE SUMS, in the middle: lock A8.tag(stage, {x: 468, y: 320, tone: 'blue', fs: 40, box: true}) with html A8.pow('7', '3', 40) + ' = 343
= 6 × 55 + 13'; unlock A8.tag(stage, {x: 468, y: 440, tone: 'green', fs: 40, box: true}) with html A8.pow('13', '27', 40) + ' mod 55 = 7'. EVE (bottom): A8.person(stage, {who: 'eve', x: 52, y: 520}); what she copied A8.tag(stage, {x: 255, y: 520, text: '(55, 3)', tone: 'red', solid: true, fs: 32}) and ({x: 385, y: 520, text: '13', ...}); her tries A8.tag(stage, {x: 500 + 104 i, y: 520, text: '÷ ' + [2,3,4,5][i], box: true, w: 92, h: 70, fs: 36, tone: 'red' (the last 'green')}) (the division sign is text); A8.tag(stage, {x: 300, y: 595, text: '55 = 5 × 11, so d = 27', tone: 'red', fs: 32}); A8.tag(stage, {x: 730, y: 595, text: 'a real n: 617 digits', tone: 'blue', solid: true, fs: 32}). DATA (assert with A8.same): A8.RSA = {n 55, e 3, d 27, M 7, powE 343, quotE 6, remE 13, C 13, back 7, attack {tries [2,3,4,5], found 5, other 11, z 40, d 27}, digits2048 617}. TIMELINE. 0.2-0.8 persons pop, the wire grows; Bob's padlock + '(55, 3)' and key + '27' pop (0.5-1.0); Eve pops at 0.6. 1.0-2.4 a blue copy of the padlock and tag leaves Bob (A8.along([[790,300],[790,190],[180,190],[180,300]], f), f = ramp(t, 1.0, 2.4, inOut)) and settles at Alice's (130, 300) / (240, 300); at 1.8 Eve's red '(55, 3)' copy pops. 3.0-3.4 Alice's grey '7' pops. 3.4-4.0 the lock sum pops (its '= 6 × 55 + 13' types out, V.type); 4.3 the '7' tile flips to the blue solid '13' with the closed purple lock; 4.5-5.4 '13' travels along the wire to Bob's spot; at 5.0 Eve's red '13' copy pops. 5.8-6.2 the unlock sum pops (key bump V.flash 5.9); 6.2-6.7 the lock opens (open 0 -> 1) and at 6.7 the tile flips to the green solid '7'. 8.4-9.6 Eve's tries pop one by one (8.4 + 0.3 i): '÷ 2', '÷ 3', '÷ 4' red with small crosses, '÷ 5' green at 9.6; 9.9 the red 'so d = 27' tag pops. 10.6 the blue '617 digits' tag pops. END STATE: Bob holds a green 7; Eve holds 55 = 5 x 11 and d = 27 (a broken toy) beside a blue tag saying a real n has 617 digits. Scene 7 starts the hash half. CAPTIONS: [[1.0,3.0,"Bob shares his public key, (55, 3)."],[3.4,5.6,"Alice locks 7 with it and gets 13."],[5.8,8.0,"Bob unlocks 13 with his private key: back to 7."],[8.3,10.2,"Eve factors the tiny n in four tries: 5 × 11."],[10.4,12.0,"A real n has 617 digits."]]

title: A hash is a
fingerprint of data
caps: A hash turns data into a short fingerprint.
The same data always gives the same fingerprint.
Change one letter and every digit changes.
And you cannot work backwards from it.
scenes.spec:
IDEA: a hash is a short fingerprint of data (lesson 8.5), using the lesson's toy hash. 'cat' -> f01dce9c; the same input again -> the same fingerprint; 'cot' (one letter changed) -> cb26b6bb, where every one of the 8 digits differs; and there is no way back from fingerprint to data. COLOURS (whole video, see the outline): blue = PUBLIC (anything Eve can see: public numbers, the public key, what crosses the wire, fingerprints); purple = SECRET (private numbers, keys and paint, always with a lock icon or a dashed purple frame); green = agreed / valid / unlocked / sealed; red = Eve and everything broken (her disc and copies, a mismatching link, a failed guess); orange = attention (what changed, the guesses being tried); grey = neutral. Grey = the data, blue = fingerprints (public), orange = the changed letter and the digits that changed, green = the same.

LAYOUT (stage px): three rows (y 100, 240, 380) of the same machine, each = input tile, arrow, 'hash' box, arrow, fingerprint. Input: A8.tag(stage, {x: 130, y, text: 'cat', box: true, tone: 'grey', fs: 44, w: 130, h: 76}); arrows const svg = L5.svg(stage); svg.append(L5.arrow(210, y, 330, y, 'grey', 1, {w: 7, head: 20})) and L5.arrow(575, y, 650, y, ...) with L5.drawOn(arrowG, k) to draw them on; machine A8.tag(stage, {x: 468, y, text: 'hash', box: true, tone: 'grey', fs: 40, w: 190, h: 76}); fingerprint A8.digest(stage, {x: 780, y, text: A8.HASH.cat, fs: 36}) .set({marks}). Row 1 y 100 'cat' -> A8.HASH.cat; row 2 y 240 'cat' again -> A8.HASH.cat with marks () => 'green' (and a green A8.icon(stage, 'equals', {x: 780, y: 170, tone: 'green', disc: true, size: 52}) between the two blue fingerprints); row 3 y 380 'cot' (tone 'orange') -> A8.HASH.cot with marks () => 'orange' (A8.HASH.diffHex lists the digits that differ: all 8). NO WAY BACK, y 540: a ghost fingerprint A8.digest(stage, {x: 790, y: 540, text: A8.HASH.cat, fs: 36}).set({ghost: true}), a red arrow L5.arrow(690, 540, 210, 540, 'red', 1, {w: 6, head: 18}), a cross A8.icon(stage, 'cross', {x: 450, y: 540, tone: 'red', disc: true, size: 56}) on it and a red A8.tag(stage, {x: 130, y: 540, text: '?', box: true, tone: 'red', fs: 44, w: 100, h: 76}).

DATA (assert): A8.HASH = {cat 'f01dce9c', cot 'cb26b6bb', diffHex [0..7], bits 18}; A8.toy('cat') must equal A8.HASH.cat.

TIMELINE. 0.2-0.7 'cat' pops; 0.6-0.9 arrow 1 draws; 0.7-1.1 'hash' pops; 1.0-1.3 arrow 2 draws; 1.3-1.9 the fingerprint pops and types out (V.type, the digest text). 2.9-3.3 row 2's 'cat' pops, 3.2-3.8 both arrows and the machine, 3.8-4.4 its fingerprint pops in green marks, 4.2 the equals disc pops. 5.1-5.5 row 3's orange 'cot' pops (the middle letter changed, flash it once), 5.5-6.2 arrows and machine, 6.2-6.8 its fingerprint types out with all 8 digits orange. 7.4-8.0 the ghost fingerprint pops, 7.7-8.4 the red arrow draws from right to left, 8.2 the cross pops, 8.6 the red '?' pops. 8.8-9.8 hold.

END STATE: three identical machines: cat -> f01dce9c twice (green equals) and cot -> cb26b6bb all orange; below, a crossed-out red arrow from a ghost fingerprint back to '?'. Scene 8 chains fingerprints. CAPTIONS: [[0.5,2.6,"A hash turns data into a short fingerprint."],[2.9,4.9,"The same data always gives the same fingerprint."],[5.1,7.2,"Change one letter and every digit changes."],[7.6,9.6,"And you cannot work backwards from it."]]

title: Edit one block and
every link after breaks
caps: Each block stores the hash of the block before it.
Edit one block and its hash changes.
The next block holds the old hash: the link breaks.
Recompute every later hash and it looks valid again.
Hashes spot edits. They do not stop them.
scenes.spec:
IDEA: a hash chain (lesson 8.5 runner). Each block stores its data, the hash of the block before it (prev) and its own hash. Edit block 1: its hash changes, so block 2's stored prev no longer matches and the link breaks; the forger repairs block 2's prev, which changes block 2's hash and breaks block 3, repairs that too, and the whole chain checks out again: hashes detect edits, they do not prevent them (that needs the work of scenes 9 and 10). A CHECK STRIP under the blocks shows what 'the link breaks' means: the prev stored in a block is compared with the hash of the block before it, digit by digit. COLOURS (whole video, see the outline): blue = PUBLIC (anything Eve can see: public numbers, the public key, what crosses the wire, fingerprints); purple = SECRET (private numbers, keys and paint, always with a lock icon or a dashed purple frame); green = agreed / valid / unlocked / sealed; red = Eve and everything broken (her disc and copies, a mismatching link, a failed guess); orange = attention (what changed, the guesses being tried); grey = neutral. Blue = hashes and links that match (public fingerprints), orange = the edited data and the digits that are changing, red = a mismatch.

LAYOUT (stage px). THREE BLOCKS: const b = [0, 1, 2].map((i) => A8.block(stage, {x: i * 333, y: 40, w: 270, title: 'Block ' + (i + 1)})) (each 270 x 226; fields data / prev / hash). Every frame: b[i].set({data: v[i].data, prev: v[i].prev, hash: v[i].hash, dataTone: v[i].edited ? 'orange' : 'grey', prevTone: v[i].linkOk ? 'blue' : 'red', hashTone: 'blue', hashMarks, tone: v[i].linkOk ? 'grey' : 'red', mark: v[i].linkOk ? null : 'bad', k, o}) with const v = A8.CHAIN.view(stage) (stage 0 honest, 1 block 1 edited, 2 block 2 repaired, 3 block 3 repaired; see the data header of common.js; hashMarks (j) => 'orange' on every digit while a hash is changing). LINKS: for i in 0, 1: const pts = A8.elbow(b[i].pt('hash', 'r'), b[i + 1].pt('prev', 'l')); A8.link(stage, {pts, tone: 'blue'}) (tone 'red' when v[i + 1].linkOk is false; k = 0..1 draws it) and a disc badge on the middle of the elbow: A8.icon(stage, 'tick', {x: pts[1][0], y: (pts[1][1] + pts[2][1]) / 2, size: 40, disc: true, tone: 'green'}) or the same with 'cross' and tone 'red' (build both, show one with set({o})). CHECK STRIP (centred at x 468): two labels A8.tag(stage, {x: 310, y: 345, text: 'stored in block ' + (L + 1), tone: 'grey'}) and ({x: 626, y: 345, text: 'hash of block ' + L}); two fingerprints A8.digest(stage, {x: 310, y: 405, fs: 36}) (the prev stored in block L + 1 = v[L].prev) and ({x: 626, y: 405, fs: 36}) (the hash of block L = v[L - 1].hash); between them a disc icon A8.icon(stage, 'tick' | 'cross', {x: 468, y: 405, size: 56, disc: true, tone: 'green' | 'red'}); when they match every digit is marked green (marks: () => 'green'), when they differ the differing digits are marked red (A8.diffIdx(stored, actual)). L = 1 (the link into block 2) until 8.6, then L = 2. VERDICT: const badge = L5.badge(stage, {x: 303, y: 500, w: 330, h: 68, valid: 'valid chain', invalid: 'broken chain'}); badge('valid' | 'invalid' | 'none', k). Last: A8.tag(stage, {x: 468, y: 596, text: 'but the edit is still there', tone: 'orange'}).

DATA (assert with A8.same): genesis hash A8.CHAIN.genesis = 'ecaf011a'. Stage 0: block 1 prev ecaf011a hash fb28ccb9; block 2 prev fb28ccb9 hash 51320862; block 3 prev 51320862 hash 57cc211e. Stage 1: block 1 'ann pays EVE 50' hash 9a1f8189 (seven of its eight digits differ from fb28ccb9), block 2 linkOk false (stored fb28ccb9 against 9a1f8189). Stage 2: block 2 prev 9a1f8189 hash 25ebb100, block 3 linkOk false (stored 51320862 against 25ebb100). Stage 3: block 3 prev 25ebb100 hash 99c1e647, all linkOk.

TIMELINE. stage = t < 3.9 ? 0 : t < 7.9 ? 1 : t < 9.8 ? 2 : 3. 0.2-1.4 the three blocks pop one by one (0.25 s apart, k = ramp). 1.5-2.4 the links draw (blue) and the green tick discs pop at 2.0-2.4. 2.2-2.6 the check strip pops: labels, the two fingerprints (both fb28ccb9, all green) and a green tick disc; 2.4 the green 'valid chain' badge pops. 3.3-3.9 block 1's data strip turns orange and its text types 'ann pays EVE 50' (V.type); 3.9-4.4 its hash digits flip to 9a1f8189 (all digits orange while they change, then blue). 5.0-5.4 the check strip's right fingerprint becomes 9a1f8189: the differing digits turn red and its disc becomes a red cross (stored fb28ccb9 against 9a1f8189); the link 1->2 turns red with a cross disc, block 2's prev strip and card turn red and its title gets the red cross (stage 1 flags); 5.5 the badge flips to red 'broken chain'. 7.9-8.5 block 2's prev changes to 9a1f8189 and its hash flips to 25ebb100 (orange while changing): the strip shows 9a1f8189 against 9a1f8189, green tick; the link 1->2 is blue with a tick. 8.6 the strip moves to L = 2 (labels and digits change): stored in block 3 51320862 against hash of block 2 25ebb100, red cross; the link 2->3 turns red / cross and block 3 goes red (stage 2 flags). 9.8-10.4 block 3's prev changes to 25ebb100 and its hash flips to 99c1e647: the strip shows 25ebb100 against 25ebb100, green tick; every link is blue with green ticks; at 10.4 the badge flips back to green 'valid chain' with a pop; 11.0 the orange tag 'but the edit is still there' pops. 11.2-12.4 hold.

Scene 9 makes forging expensive. They do not stop them."]]

title: Sealing a block
means guessing
caps: Try numbers (nonces) until the hash starts with 0.
Every try gives a new, unpredictable hash.
Found it after 15 hashes. Checking takes just 1.
Each extra zero makes a hit 16 times rarer.
So it costs about 16 times more work.
scenes.spec:
IDEA: proof of work (lesson 8.7 runner). To seal block 7 ('cat pays dan 4') a miner changes the NONCE (just a number to try) and hashes again until the hash starts with 0. Nothing predicts which nonce works, so it is pure guessing: here nonce 14 wins after 15 hashes. Checking the winner costs ONE hash. One hash in 16 starts with 0; each extra zero makes a hit 16 times rarer (1 in 256 for 00), so it costs about 16 times more work. COLOURS (whole video, see the outline): blue = PUBLIC (anything Eve can see: public numbers, the public key, what crosses the wire, fingerprints); purple = SECRET (private numbers, keys and paint, always with a lock icon or a dashed purple frame); green = agreed / valid / unlocked / sealed; red = Eve and everything broken (her disc and copies, a mismatching link, a failed guess); orange = attention (what changed, the guesses being tried); grey = neutral. Orange = the target and the guesses being tried, red = a failed try, green = the winner / the check.

LAYOUT (stage px). THE BLOCK BEING SEALED: const blk = A8.block(stage, {x: 0, y: 10, w: 300, fields: ['data', 'nonce', 'hash'], title: 'Block 7'}); blk.set({data: 'cat pays dan 4', nonce: row.n, hash: row.hash, hashTone: 'blue' | 'green', hashMarks: (j) => j === 0 ? (row.ok ? 'green' : 'red') : null, mark: row.ok ? 'ok' : null}) where row = A8.MINE.rows[floor(try)] (the card shows the current try). THE LOG: const tr = A8.tries(stage, {x: 340, y: 10, w: 590, rows: 5, rowH: 62, count: A8.MINE.rows.length, lead: true, row: (i) => ({a: 'nonce ' + A8.MINE.rows[i].n, b: A8.MINE.rows[i].hash, ok: A8.MINE.rows[i].ok})}); tr.update({upto, hi, hiK}) (upto = rows revealed, hi 14 for the winner). TARGET: A8.tag(stage, {x: 150, y: 285, text: 'hash starts with 0', tone: 'orange'}). WINNER: A8.tag(stage, {x: 640, y: 350, text: 'found after 15 hashes', tone: 'green', solid: true}). WORK BARS (bottom): A8.bar(stage, {x: 20, y: 430, w: 360, tone: 'orange'}) set({k: 1, text: 'find: 15 hashes'}) and A8.bar(stage, {x: 20, y: 500, w: 360, tone: 'green'}) set({k: 1 / 15, text: 'check: 1 hash', textOut: true}) (a bar of 15 units against a bar of 1). THE ODDS (a second figure that takes over the whole stage once the first has faded): const g = A8.cells(stage, {x: 60, y: 130, cols: 16, rows: 16, size: 20, gap: 4}) (a 380 x 380 square at x 60..440, y 130..510; its first row is the 16-cell strip), g.update((r, c) => r === 0 && c === 5 ? {tone: 'green'} : undefined, {rows, cols}) with rows = 1 and cols = 16 * ramp(...) while the strip builds, then rows = 1 + 15 * ramp(...) (fractional rows / cols pop in), tags (left-anchored in a column at x 480): A8.tag(stage, {x: 480, y: 142, text: 'starts with 0: 1 in 16', tone: 'orange', anchor: 'l'}), A8.tag(stage, {x: 480, y: 330, text: 'starts with 00: 1 in 256', tone: 'orange', anchor: 'l'}), A8.tag(stage, {x: 480, y: 470, text: '16 times more work', tone: 'orange', solid: true, fs: 36, anchor: 'l'}).

DATA (assert with A8.same): A8.MINE = {data 'block 7', text 'cat pays dan 4', target '0', win 14, tries 15, chance 16, rows [{n 0, hash 'cfc7cb5a', ok false} ... {n 14, hash '0d84059e', ok true}], checkCost 1}; A8.ZEROS = [{zeros 1, odds 16, cells 16}, {zeros 2, odds 256, cells 256}].

TIMELINE. 0.2-1.0 the block card pops (nonce 0, hash of try 0), the empty log frame appears, 0.6-1.0 the orange target tag pops. 1.2-5.7 the hunt: upto = 15 * ramp(t, 1.2, 5.7, lin) (0.3 s per try), the card's nonce and hash follow the newest row (floor(upto - 1e-9)), each failed row gets its red first-digit mark and cross. 5.7-6.2 the winner row turns green (hi 14, hiK ramp 5.7-6.2), the card turns green with a tick; 6.2 the green 'found after 15 hashes' tag pops. 6.8-7.5 the orange bar 'find: 15 hashes' grows (k ramp 6.8-7.5), 7.5-7.9 the green 'check: 1 hash' bar pops (k = 1/15, text outside) with a small tick. 8.4-8.8 the bars, the 'found' tag, the block card, the log and the target tag all fade out (o). 8.8-9.4 the first row of 16 cells pops in from the left (cols = 16 * ramp(t, 8.8, 9.4, lin), rows = 1) with one green cell; the tag 'starts with 0: 1 in 16' pops 9.2. 9.8-11.0 rows 2 to 16 pop in (rows = 1 + 15 * ramp(t, 9.8, 11.0, lin)) while the one green cell stays the only one; 11.0 the tag 'starts with 00: 1 in 256' pops; 11.4 the orange solid '16 times more work' pops. 11.6-13.2 hold.

END STATE: a 16 x 16 square of pale cells with a single green one and, in a column on its right, the two odds tags and the '16 times more work' sticker. Scene 10 uses this work to protect a chain. title: Rewriting history
means redoing the work
caps: Each block is sealed by its own proof of work.

scenes.spec:
IDEA: a chain whose blocks are each sealed by mining. Editing block 1 breaks its own seal (its hash no longer starts with 0) and the stored prev of block 2; repairing means mining block 1 again (15 tries), then block 2 with the new prev (5 tries), then block 3 (30 tries): 50 tries to forge three blocks, where scene 8's forger needed none. At real difficulty each hunt is astronomically bigger, which is what protects history. COLOURS (whole video, see the outline): blue = PUBLIC (anything Eve can see: public numbers, the public key, what crosses the wire, fingerprints); purple = SECRET (private numbers, keys and paint, always with a lock icon or a dashed purple frame); green = agreed / valid / unlocked / sealed; red = Eve and everything broken (her disc and copies, a mismatching link, a failed guess); orange = attention (what changed, the guesses being tried); grey = neutral. Green = sealed and linked, red = broken seal or link, orange = the edit and the work being done.

LAYOUT (stage px). THREE BLOCKS: const b = [0, 1, 2].map((i) => A8.block(stage, {x: i * 333, y: 10, w: 270, fields: ['data', 'prev', 'nonce', 'hash'], title: 'Block ' + (i + 1)})) (each 270 x 280). Every frame b[i].set({data: v[i].data, prev: v[i].prev, nonce: v[i].nonce, hash: v[i].hash, dataTone: v[i].edited ? 'orange' : 'grey', prevTone: v[i].linkOk ? 'blue' : 'red', hashTone: 'blue', hashMarks: (j) => j === 0 ? (v[i].sealOk ? 'green' : 'red') : null, mark: v[i].sealOk && v[i].linkOk ? 'ok' : 'bad', tone: v[i].linkOk ? 'grey' : 'red', k, o}) with const v = A8.SEAL.view(stage) (stage 0 sealed, 1 block 1 edited with its old nonce, 2 block 1 re-mined, 3 block 2 re-mined, 4 block 3 re-mined; during a hunt show the current try instead: nonce = n and hash = A8.SEAL.hunt(i).rows[n] of the block being mined, with the leading digit red until the last try). WORK BARS: for i in 0..2 a label A8.tag(stage, {x: 20, y: 354 + 60 i, text: 'block ' + (i + 1), anchor: 'l'}) and a bar A8.bar(stage, {x: 175, y: 330 + 60 i, w: 340, tone: 'orange'}) with k = tries / 30 (15 / 30, 5 / 30, 30 / 30), text 'N tries' inside (block 2 is short: textOut: true). TOTAL: A8.tag(stage, {x: 740, y: 420, text: '50 tries', tone: 'orange', solid: true, fs: 44}).

DATA (assert with A8.same): A8.SEAL.original = nonces 27 / 24 / 16, hashes 017b7e46 / 0b2e58f5 / 006f9014 (tries 28 / 25 / 17); A8.SEAL.forged = block 1 'ann pays EVE 50' nonce 14 hash 03fbf4ca (15 tries), block 2 nonce 4 hash 06ab4a15 (5 tries), block 3 nonce 29 hash 0e76a113 (30 tries); A8.SEAL.total = 50. Stage 1: [27 'b411b36a' sealOk false linkOk true], [24 '0b2e58f5' true false], [16 '006f9014' true true].

TIMELINE. 0.2-1.4 the three sealed blocks pop (stage 0; green leading zeros, green ticks), 0.25 s apart. 2.0-2.6 block 1's data turns orange and types 'ann pays EVE 50' (V.type); 2.6-3.1 its hash flips to b411b36a (stage 1) with a red first digit and a red cross; 3.1-3.5 block 2's prev strip and card turn red. 4.0-5.4 hunt 1: nonce counts 0..14 through A8.SEAL.hunt(1).rows (about 0.09 s per row), the bar for block 1 grows to 15 / 30, at 5.4 block 1 turns green (stage 2); block 2 stays red. 5.8-6.6 block 2's prev changes to 03fbf4ca, hunt 2: nonce 0..4 (0.16 s per row), its bar grows to 5 / 30, at 6.6 green (stage 3); block 3's prev strip turns red. 6.8-8.4 block 3's prev changes to 06ab4a15, hunt 3: nonce 0..29 (0.05 s per row), its bar grows to 30 / 30, at 8.4 green (stage 4). 8.6-9.0 the orange '50 tries' sticker pops (bump). 9.0-10.7 hold.

END STATE: three green sealed blocks (nonces 14 / 4 / 29), three orange work bars 15 / 5 / 30 and the '50 tries' total. The edit is still orange in block 1. The recap follows. CAPTIONS: [[0.5,2.0,"Each block is sealed by its own proof of work."],[2.2,4.0,"Edit block 1: its seal and the link both break."],[4.2,6.2,"Forging it means mining block 1 again."],[6.4,8.4,"Then every later block must be mined again too."],[8.8,10.7,"Rewriting history means redoing all that work."]]

helpers:
FILES: videos/a8/common.js (pure data and algorithms, no DOM; every number asserted at load), videos/a8/common-2.js (A8.tag, A8.person, A8.icon, A8.wire, A8.pot, A8.drop, A8.link, A8.arc, A8.along, A8.pow, A8.textW), videos/a8/common-3.js (A8.digest, A8.block, A8.elbow, A8.tries, A8.cells, A8.bar). Everything hangs off window.VID.a8; scenes start with const V = window.VID, A8 = V.a8, L5 = V.l5 and const {ramp, flash, clamp, lerp, ease: E} = V. videos/algo-8.html loads engine.js, cards.js, l5/common.js, a8/common.js, common-2.js, common-3.js, scene-01 ... scene-11, audio/algo-8.js. l6 is not loaded. Every file starts with a long API comment: READ THEM FIRST, they are the contract. Every set() / update() is pure: call it each frame from update(t) with everything you want to see; nothing is remembered; no Math.random, Date or timers. A. DATA (common.js): A8.CIPHER, A8.PAINT, A8.DH, A8.BIG, A8.RSA, A8.HASH, A8.CHAIN (genesis, edit, view(stage)), A8.MINE, A8.ZEROS, A8.SEAL (original, forged, view(stage), hunt(blockNo), total, totalOriginal); tools A8.toy, A8.modpow, A8.gcd, A8.caesar, A8.diffIdx, A8.commas, A8.same / A8.close / A8.must. B. SMALL PIECES (common-2.js): A8.tag(parent, {x, y, text | html, tone, solid, fs, mono, box, w, h, anchor 'c' | 'l' | 'r' | 'tl'}) -> .set({text, html, tone, solid, ghost, x, y, dx, dy, s, r, o, k}) (x, y = centre by default; k pops it in; text may contain \n; html for A8.pow expressions and
); A8.person(parent, {who 'alice' | 'bob' | 'eve', x, y, r 38, name 'right' | 'left' | 'below' | 'none'}); A8.icon(parent, 'lock' | 'key' | 'eye' | 'qmark' | 'plus' | 'equals' | 'tick' | 'cross' | 'arrow', {x, y, size 56, tone, disc}) -> .set({..., k, draw (tick / cross / arrow draw-on), open (lock 0..1)}); A8.wire(parent, {x, y, w, h}) -> .set({k, o}); A8.pot(parent, {x, y, r}) -> .set({drops ['P', 'A'], frame 'purple' | 'blue', frameK, ghost, ...}) (colour = average of the paints; same for any order); A8.drop(parent, {x, y, r, paint}); A8.link(parent, {pts, tone, w, head}) -> .set({k, tone, o, dash}); A8.arc(p, q, f, bend) and A8.along(pts, f) -> {x, y}; A8.pow(base, exp, fs) -> html with the exponent raised (>= 28 px); A8.textW(text, fs, mono). C. BIGGER PIECES (common-3.js): A8.digest(parent, {x, y, text, tone, fs 32}) -> .set({text, marks: (i, ch) => tone | null, ghost, ...}) (marks highlight single hex digits); A8.block(parent, {x, y, w 270, fields ['data', 'prev', 'nonce', 'hash'], title}) -> .set({title, data, prev, nonce, hash, dataTone, prevTone, nonceTone, hashTone, hashMarks, prevMarks, tone, mark 'ok' | 'bad', ...}), .pt(field, 'l' | 'r') for link ends; A8.elbow(p, q) -> pts for A8.link; A8.tries(parent, {x, y, w, rows, rowH, count, row: (i) => {a, b, ok}, lead}) -> .update({upto, hi, hiK, o}) (a scrolling table of tries); A8.cells(parent, {x, y, cols, rows, size, gap}) -> .update((r, c) => undefined | {k, tone, ghost}, {o}); A8.bar(parent, {x, y, w, h, tone, text}) -> .set({k, tone, solid, text, textOut, o}). D. REUSED FROM videos/l5/common.js (V.l5): L5.tone(name), L5.tick, L5.cross, L5.arrow(x1, y1, x2, y2, tone, o, {w, head, bow}) + L5.drawOn(g, k) + L5.svg(parent) (a full-stage SVG), L5.badge(parent, {x, y, w, h, valid, invalid}) -> badge('valid' | 'invalid' | 'none', k), L5.chromosome(parent, {x, y, genes, size, gap, tone}) for the letter tiles of scene 2 (.set(i, {x, y, s, o, tone, text}), .flip(i, k, {from, to, tone, toTone}), .all(fn)). Do NOT use L5.tourMap. E. RULES: no white colours (var(--panel) / var(--bg)); labels >= 28 px; everything >= 12 px inside the 936 x 640 stage; update(t) pure; assert every number you show against the storyboard with A8.same(...) when the scene is built (or read it straight from the A8 data); each file < 500 code lines (split a long scene into helpers in the same file or a second part named scene-NN--b.js listed in algo-8.html); run npx prettier --write and npx eslint on every file you touch. Stills: node tools/video-still.js algo-8 s4@6,s4@12 /tmp/ (scene number @ local seconds). F. THINGS TO KNOW. (1) A8.tag text is escaped; to show a raised exponent or
pass html. (2) Typing text: tag.set({text: V.type(full, k)}). (3) The a8 digest and block cells are monospace; a block card's top row is the title (30 px) and its mark (tick / cross) at the right. (4) A8.block.set({x, y}) are TOP-LEFT coordinates; every other handle's x, y are CENTRES. (5) A8.pot colours need the page's CSS tokens, which exist when build() runs. (6) The paint colours are the only literal colours; everywhere else colour = role. (7) Mining / hunt rows: A8.SEAL.hunt(i).rows are the digests of nonce 0..win for the block being mined (i = 1, 2, 3). (8) Placeholder scene files carry the right kicker, title, duration and captions: keep them (the captions come from this storyboard).
